To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aprotinin reduces postoperative blood and haemoglobin losses in primary cardiac surgery, and that a dose of one‐third that of the currently recommended regimen is effective.

(1) aprotinin significantly decreases postoperative blood loss and chest drain haemoglobin loss in primary cardiac surgical patients; (2) aprotinin is equally effective in reducing blood loss when administered as a patient bolus, as part of a prime, or as a combination of both regimens; and (3) aprotinin can be administered in a significantly decreased dose (approximately one‐third of currently recommended dosage) and still maintain its efficacy.
aprotinin significantly reduced postoperative chest drain blood loss and blood product requirements, but that the effect was dose‐dependent.

the use of the serine proteinase aprotinin to reduce the amount of blood loss during cardiac surgery.
the use of aprotinin, a serine proteinase inhibiting drug.
the study of the effects of the proteinase inhibitor a protease on the reduction of postoperative blood loss and the prevention of postoperative complications in cardiac surgery.

aprotinin is a useful agent in the treatment of postoperative bleeding in patients requiring cardiopulmonary by‐pass.
the dose of a protease inhibitor can be reduced by 2–3 orders of magnitude and still achieve significant clinical benefit in cardiac surgery.
aprotinin, at any dose, is effective in reducing blood loss in patients undergoing cardiopulmonary‐bypass surgery.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to reduce the amount of blood loss and transfusions in our cardiac patients by the use of aprotinin.
the use of aprotinin in cardiac surgery reduces blood transfusion, reduces the risk of post‐operative complications and reduces hospital costs.
aprotinin is an effective antifibrinolytic agent that reduces blood loss in cardiac surgical procedures.

aprotinin can be given at a lower dose than is currently recommended and still have the same beneficial effects.
the dose of a protinin can be reduced significantly and still obtain the benefits of aprotinin in terms of reduced blood loss and blood transfusion.
the use of aprotinin is not associated with any increase in the incidence of thrombosis or thromboembolic events.
